items.title: feat(id-caps): host-side policy point for the MCP bridge (spike #6300 step 4, #7916)
items.body: Refs #7916 — spike step 4/5 for #6300 (policy point), after step 2's bridge (PR #13161). ## What lands New `id_caps::mcp_policy` module: the host-side policy point the bridge's module docs defer to. A `PolicySession` wraps a `BridgeSession` and runs every agent tool call through the design's order (#6300 §§6–7): 1. **Capability ceiling** set at role grant — tools, worlds, object classes, program-invoke allowlist. Anything outside is refused, audited, and never reaches the bridge. 2. **Per-session quota** (local budget per §9.3, not waiting on F12.10) over frames / tool calls / program invocations, charged *before* execution. A charge that would exceed the budget refuses the action and parks the agent; parking surfaces to the driver as the first-class world event `agent parked, quota exhausted`. `world.leave` is never refused — the exit is charged nothing and still audited. 3. **Audit**: exactly one event per action, refusals and stale-input rejections included, hash-chained and signed with the host's journal key (ed25519, house style). `verify_audit_chain` checks sequence, links, hashes, and signatures end-to-end. The stale-decision rule is enforced here: a `screen_revision` token naming anything but the latest observed revision is refused as stale input. The agent is the subject, never the editor — log and spend are read-only from the session API. Owner summary renders actions / spend / refusals in the §7 shape. `program.invoke` arrives with step 5; the policy point already enforces its allowlist and charges its quota axis (an admitted invoke currently ends as an audited bridge refusal, charge standing). ## Verification - `cargo test -p id-caps --lib` in `nix develop` (pkgs/id, laptop worktree at this head): **249 passed / 0 failed**, including 9 new `mcp_policy` tests named against #7916's acceptance criteria (ceiling refusal audited + never executed; quota parking visible + summary; chain verifies end-to-end, tamper/link/signature attacks fail; stale-input rejection; object-class ceiling; program allowlist + program-axis charge; serde round-trip still verifies; no-mutation API shape). - `cargo clippy -p id-caps --lib`: zero findings in the new files (crate total went 177 → 172 pre-existing warnings; the 26 denied-lint errors in `library_attach.rs` tests under `--all-targets` are the pre-existing #803 set, untouched). - `cargo fmt -p id-caps` applied. - A dispatch-first attempt was made (run 45151325339); it failed before any code ran on the known #13159 container gap (`nixbld` group missing), so verification ran on the laptop per the established pkgs/id route. ```json { "direct_parent": null, "links": [], "lineage": { "design": null, "roadmap_item": null, "priority": null }, "pm_meta": 1, "provenance": { "queue_id": null, "scheduled_start": null, "picked_up_at": null, "work_started_at": null, "created_at": "2026-11-23T10:32:13Z", "session_id": null, "lane": null, "host": "amd", "worktree": null, "model": null, "lane_start_issues": [], "workspace_ref": null, "auth_subject": "oc-code-08", "stamped_by": "fleet 0.1.0 (native)" } } ``` --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: id(phase-14): spike step 5/5 — program.invoke through the policy point + scripted spike run
items.body: Spike step 5/5 for the id phase-14 spike (#6300): bounded program interaction, exercised end to end by a scripted spike run. ## What lands - **`program.invoke` joins the bridge's v1 tool surface** (`id_caps::mcp_bridge`, now eight tools): one call becomes exactly one `input` frame carrying the invocation's argument payload as the program's participant input, plus the caller's `screen_revision` when given. Program and object names are validated for presence only — the allowlist decision stays at the policy point, and the audit event takes the program name from the same arguments. - **The policy point admits it** (`id_caps::mcp_policy`): the step-4 boundary ("every `program.invoke` is refused until the interaction lands") is replaced — the ceiling allowlist is checked, the program axis of the quota is charged before execution, and the invocation is audited like every other action. - **The scripted spike run** (`pkgs/id/tests/mcp_spike_e2e.rs`): an agent joins a local tic-tac-toe world over iroh, driven entirely through the policy point — join, screen reads, subscribe, chat with a second participant, one ceiling-refused invoke of an unlisted program, one admitted invoke of the named program on the named object, the result read back as a semantic diff (`input_applied`, board `----X----`), leave. Oracles: the signed audit chain (nine events in script order, one refusal, chain verifies), the owner summary (9 actions / 8 executed / 1 refusal; spend frames 4, tool calls 7, program invocations 1), and the host journal exported through the fixture recorder (chats at sequences 2 and 3, the invocation's input at sequence 4). ## Finding recorded in the test A commit's frames are generated together but their wire order is not contractual: a re-rendered view can land behind the semantic diff. A driver that takes the `screen_revision` token from a partially drained stream can lag the host's current revision by exactly that trailing view, and the stale-decision gate refuses the invoke (observed live: `stale decision: input was decided against screen revision 0, current is 1`). The spike driver drains its own chat to quiescence before taking the token; the helper's doc comment carries the reasoning. ## Verification Laptop route (`nix develop` in `pkgs/id`) — the fleet-build dispatch container cannot run these suites (the #13159-family environment gaps), so the laptop is the verifying route: - `cargo test -p id-caps --lib` — 251 passed, 0 failed - `cargo test -p id-caps --test mcp_bridge_surface --test agent_policy_point` — 3/3 and 13/13 - `cargo test --test mcp_spike_e2e` — passed 4 consecutive runs - `cargo test --test mcp_bridge_e2e` — 1/1 (step-3 run unaffected) - `cargo test -p id-worlds shell_contract` — 20 passed, 0 failed (shell + agent-profile conformance suite; results also recorded on #6300) - `cargo fmt -p id-caps -- --check` clean; no new clippy diagnostics in the touched files (the crate's pre-existing denied-lint errors are the #803 slice, untouched) Closes #7917 ```json { "direct_parent": null, "links": [], "lineage": { "design": null, "roadmap_item": null, "priority": null }, "pm_meta": 1, "provenance": { "queue_id": null, "scheduled_start": null, "picked_up_at": null, "work_started_at": null, "created_at": "2026-11-23T11:52:09Z", "session_id": null, "lane": null, "host": "amd", "worktree": "/home/user/wt-lane-rv-7917", "model": null, "lane_start_issues": [], "workspace_ref": { "kind": "worktree", "id": "/home/user/wt-lane-rv-7917", "repo": "developing-today/code", "branch": "lane-rv-7917", "sha": "2504b765c79f8dca1bfefa2a0084e0c79519adaa" }, "auth_subject": "oc-code-05", "stamped_by": "fleet 0.1.0 (native)" } } ``` --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: feat(id-caps): host-side policy point for agent frames (spike 4/5, #7916)
items.body: Spike step 4 of 5 for #6300 (issue #7916): the host-side policy point for agent frames, per `doc/2026-11-09_design_id6300_agents_in_worlds_v1.md` §6, §7, §9.3. Steps 1–3 (#7913, #7914, #7915) are all closed as completed, so the design's sequencing gate for this step is clear. **New module `pkgs/id/crates/id-caps/src/agent_policy.rs`** — additive only; no existing API changes: - **Ceiling (§6.1)** — `Ceiling::from_grant` derives the tool keys from the verified join grant's scopes (presence / screen.read / chat.post / program.invoke), in the grant's world; object classes and the program allowlist are owner-side additions. Anything outside is refused before anything else happens. - **Quota (§6.2, §9.3)** — per-session budget over frames / tool calls / program invocations, charged *before* execution and refused atomically. Exhaustion parks the session and emits the first-class `agent_parked` world event ("agent parked, quota exhausted") in the local-budget shape F12.10 will consume; a parked session refuses everything after. - **Guardrails (§4.3, §6.3)** — stale-decision rejection (decided-against revision must still be current) and per-tool rate limits (chat.post's limit is part of the role), plus delegation-expiry refusal. - **Audit (§7)** — one event per action including refusals and stale-input rejections (agent, owner, world, tool, object, proof ref, quota charged, outcome), hash-chained and host-signed; `verify_events` re-derives the whole chain so any edit is detected. The agent is never the editor: the log appends only inside the policy point. `OwnerSummary` renders the owner-facing line (actions, spend, refusals). **Verification** — `crates/id-caps/tests/agent_policy_point.rs`: 13 tests named for the acceptance criteria (out-of-ceiling refused/audited/never executed; refusals never sampled away; parking visible; charge-before-execution; chain verifies and detects tampering; stale-input rejected; summary contents; allowlist + program axis; object classes; rate-limit window; expiry; join is event #1; mixed-sequence completeness property). items.title: id-shell contract revision 11: agent profile — region subscriptions, semantic diffs, stale-decision token (#7913)
items.body: Implements #7913 (spike 1/5 for #6300): the agent shell profile in the id-shell contract, per design `doc/2026-11-09_design_id6300_agents_in_worlds_v1.md` sections 4.2, 4.3, 8, 9.1 (PR #7911). ## Contract (additive revision 10 -> 11) - `join` gains the `agent_profile` capability flag: a shell that sets it advertises it can consume semantic diffs. - New client frame `screen_subscribe` (ephemeral, joined): a screen region and/or semantic event classes (`chat_posted`, `input_applied`, `object_changed`, `system_event`, `program_changed`; empty list = all, absent = none). - New server frames `semantic_diff` (ephemeral) and `screen_subscription` (reply, echoes the active subscription + current screen revision). - Agent input frames (`input`, `chat`, `paste`, `form_result`, `pointer`) gain the optional `screen_revision` stale-decision token. - `features.agent_profile` documents the profile, including the reduced-fidelity rule: a host without the revision serves an agent full view frames with identical authority. ## Host (id-worlds) - Join threads `agent_profile` into the session's view state; authority is unchanged. - `screen_subscribe` is validated (region bounds, known classes, at least one of region/classes, agent flag required), recorded connection-locally, and answered with `screen_subscription`. - Subscribed event classes arrive as `semantic_diff` frames in world terms (chat text, object ref, program hash — never raw input bytes, system payloads, or seeds). - Region subscribers get `region_changed` diffs computed in `send_view` against the last screen the session received, scoped to the subscribed rows/columns. - Stale-decision gate: an input whose `screen_revision` is not the session's current screen revision is rejected before dispatch with an `error` frame (code `stale_decision`), commits nothing, and the current view follows. ## Native shell (id-native-shell) - Builders: `agent_join_frame`, `screen_subscribe_frame`, `input_frame_with_revision`. - `SessionState` folds `semantic_diff` / `screen_subscription` frames; `semantic_diff_text` renders diffs as world-term lines. ## Conformance (design section 8 cases for this spike) - Contract parity + transcript tests (shell_contract): agent-profile session conforms; subscription is joined-only; a diff may not leak a seed. - Live host tests (world_session contract_tests): scoped diffs delivered, unsubscribed classes and region-only subscriptions leak nothing, stale input rejected with no commit, current input commits exactly one event, human sessions get no agent frames. - Region scoping + subscription scoping unit oracles (view.rs); native-shell transcript conformance + semantic-diff rendering test. Also fixes the pre-existing main breakage filed as #11277 (id-worlds did not compile at e5eab191: revision-10 Pointer/Hover dispatch missing, E0004 x2 — proven on a clean worktree; plus two test-build import/shadowing errors behind it). Interim dispatch: hover = ephemeral no-op, pointer = explicit `input_refused`/`unknown_or_unsupported_event` until #1831 routing lands; the journal-boundary test's pointer expectation is written ahead of that routing and stays red for #1831. Queue: task 20044, lane any-e. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(id-caps): agent identity, role binding, UCAN-style delegation spike (#7915)
items.body: ## Spike 3/5 for #6300 — agent identity, roles, UCAN-style attenuated delegation Implements issue #7915 per `doc/2026-11-09_design_id6300_agents_in_worlds_v1.md` §5, §9.2, §9.4 (design delivered by PR #7911). New self-contained module `id_caps::agent_delegation` (pkgs/id/crates/id-caps), reusing the existing `WorldScopes` capability set. Nothing existing is modified beyond the one-line module registration. ### What lands - **Agent identity (§5.1):** `AgentId` is the agent's own Ed25519 public key (the iroh endpoint ID); the key alone grants nothing. - **Role binding (§5.2):** `Role` = capability ceiling + worlds + lifetime; `RoleBinding` is the owner's Ed25519 signature binding an agent key to a role in one world. - **Delegation (§5.2):** `Delegation::issue` mints depth-1, expiring, offline-verifiable tokens; scopes must attenuate the binding ceiling (checked at issuance *and* re-derived at verification, so even an owner-signed widened token fails). - **Lifetime & renewal (§5.3, §9.2):** 1 h default; role lifetimes bounded to 15 min – 4 h; `Delegation::renew` succeeds only for the binding owner's key — the agent cannot renew its own token (stopping renewal is revocation). - **Join verification (§5.2, §7):** `verify_join` re-derives every check from the two signatures (binding signature, issuer = owner, depth = 1, world/role/agent match, delegation signature, ceiling, expiry); `verify_join_audited` also emits the §7 audit event (agent, owner, world, tool, proof reference, outcome) for grants *and* refusals. - **Hosted edge (§5.4, §9.4):** `EdgeScopes` parses `world: role:`; `authorize_edge` re-derives authority from binding + chain — a valid transport token with no matching role binding grants nothing. ### Acceptance tests (oracle: the design doc) `cargo test -p id-caps agent_delegation` — 8 passed: - join without a valid chain is refused and audited (§5.2, §7) - valid chain grants exactly the delegated scopes (§5.2) - widened token fails verification; issuance refuses to mint it (§5.2, §4.5.1) - re-delegated (depth-2 / agent-signed) token fails (§5.2) - expired token fails (§5.3) - renewal is owner-client-only (§5.3, §9.2) - lifetime bounds enforced, 1 h default (§9.2) - hosted edge: valid token, no role binding → grants nothing (§5.4, §9.4) Full `id-caps` suite: 147 passed, 0 failed. `cargo fmt` clean. (Clippy could not run in this worktree: the shared target cache was built by an incompatible rustc — E0514 on dependency crates, unrelated to this change.) ### Assumptions / scope notes - The audit event uses the §7 field shape (spike 4 / #7916, the policy point, is still open and will own journaling; this spike returns the event rather than writing a journal). - The module is the spike's proving ground: wiring `verify_join` into the live world join path is follow-on work once spike 4 lands the policy point. Queue task 20045, lane any-n. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: feat(id-caps): MCP bridge translator + end-to-end world session (#7914 criterion 1)
items.body: For #7914 — this lands criterion 1, the last open acceptance criterion. (The PR body deliberately carries the closing reference below: criteria 2 and 3 landed with PR #12917, and criterion 1 is proven by the new end-to-end test in this PR.) ## What lands **The bridge translator** (`id_caps::mcp_bridge`, design #6300 sections 3 and 4.4). `BridgeSession` now translates each of the seven pinned v1 tool calls into the bridge driver's next step: - `world.join` → the agent-profile `join` frame (mirrors the native shell's `agent_join_frame` shape) - `screen.subscribe` → the `screen_subscribe` frame (region and/or event classes, validated) - `chat.post` → the `chat` frame, with the caller's stale-decision token when supplied (section 4.3) - `screen.read` → answered locally from the observed frames: latest full view text plus the semantic-diff changes since the previous read (reading drains them; patch views never blank the screen) - `object.inspect` → answered locally from the `object_changed` changes observed so far - `world.leave` → `ToolAction::Close` (presence in the F13.1 contract is connection-scoped; there is no leave frame) - `presence.set` → refused with the typed `BridgeError::NoFrameMapping` — the contract carries presence only as the join itself, so there is no presence frame to send Session state is enforced bridge-side: session tools refuse before a join (`NotJoined`), a second join is refused (`AlreadyJoined`), unknown tools are refused (`UnknownTool`), and a definition mismatch terminates translation (`Terminated`). **The end-to-end proof** (`pkgs/id/tests/mcp_bridge_e2e.rs`, covered by the facade test glob in the suite registry — no registry edit needed): a live `WorldService` host (tic-tac-toe installed) served over iroh on loopback. The agent side is driven purely by tool calls through the translator; a second participant joins raw and posts chat. The test proves: join delivers a view the bridge renders; the subscription is acked; the other participant's chat arrives as a pushed `semantic_diff` and surfaces through `screen.read` exactly once; the agent's `chat.post` lands as the durable event at sequence 3; `world.leave` closes; and the host journal (admin fixture record) holds both chats in order with `current_sequence` 3. The facade gains an `iroh-blobs` dev-dependency (already in the lock as a normal dependency; `Cargo.lock` unchanged) for the test host's in-memory blob store. ## Verification - `cargo test -p id-caps` — 216 lib tests (10 new translator unit tests) + 3 surface tests, all green; the surface suite gains a coverage test: every surface tool translates or names its missing mapping, and the five forbidden non-tools never translate. - `cargo test --test mcp_bridge_e2e` — 1 passed (2.11s). - `cargo fmt` — the changed files are fmt-clean (the workspace has 49 pre-existing fmt diffs in unrelated files on main; untouched here). - `cargo clippy -p id-caps --all-targets` — no findings in the new code; the run still fails on 26 pre-existing deny-lint errors in `library_attach.rs` test code and one pre-existing warning in `definition_hash`, both untouched by this PR and present on main. Closes #7914 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

### Tokio broadcast channel calls clone in parallel, but does not require `Sync`
[GHSA-rr8g-9fpq-6wmg](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-rr8g-9fpq-6wmg)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
The broadcast channel internally calls `clone` on the stored value when receiving it, and only requires `T:Send`. This means that using the broadcast channel with values that are `Send` but not `Sync` can trigger unsoundness if the `clone` implementation makes use of the value being `!Sync`.

Thank you to Austin Bonander for finding and reporting this issue.
